implementation_notes: The filter is a zero-cost lazy adapter: `iter.filter(pred)` yields only the values the predicate accepts (`FnMut(&Item) -> bool`), `filter_map` merges criterion and conversion, and `partition` splits accepted and rejected in a single pass - which is how rejects are preserved instead of silently dropped; `Vec::retain` is the in-place form for buffered messages. A runtime-configurable criterion is stored as `Box<dyn Fn(&Message) -> bool>` (or a trait object) when it comes from configuration and must be swappable.
pitfalls: Iterator::filter's predicate borrows each item (`&Item`), so a criterion that needs ownership must use filter_map or partition, which move the values.
Vec::retain drops rejected values immediately and its closure sees only `&T`: count or collect rejects before retaining if they matter.
A filter closure that updates a counter needs a mutable borrow, which conflicts with the iterator's borrow of the source; use Cell/atomic counters or a separate pass.

variants.name: Async stream filter (futures StreamExt)
variants.implementation_notes: For messages arriving asynchronously, `StreamExt::filter` is the streaming realization: the predicate is `FnMut(&Item) -> Fut` with `Fut: Future<Output = bool>`, so a criterion may await (call a policy service, refresh a credential) without blocking the executor, and non-matching items are never yielded downstream; `try_filter`/`filter_map` cover validating and converting criteria. Use it in tokio/async-std pipelines; plain iterators remain simpler for in-memory feeds.
pitfalls: The predicate returns a future, so capturing the item across await points fights the borrow checker - decide whether the criterion needs the owned message or only a header.
StreamExt must be in scope and the stream is consumed by the adapter chain; `boxed()` converts it to a pinned trait object and adds an allocation per stage.
Awaiting inside the filter serialises one policy call per item; without `buffered`/`buffer_unordered` throughput collapses to the service's latency.
